citation.title: Confidence Intervals for Linear Unbiased Estimators under Constrained Dependence

standing_assumptions:
The article is Electronic Journal of Statistics 12 (2018) 2238–2252. Printed page = PDF page + 2237 (printed p. 2240 is PDF p. 3). Everything quoted from the article was read from the page images (staged/pages/p-NN.png, re-rendered at 200 dpi for the formulas).
(S1) Graph and dependency graph. p. 2240 (PDF p. 3): "Consider a simple graph $\mathcal G = (\mathcal V, \mathcal E)$ with no parallel edges or self-loops. Let $|\mathcal V| = N$. Associated with each vertex $i \in \mathcal V$ is a random variable $Y_i$, and $\mathcal G$ characterizes probabilistic dependencies in the outcomes [e.g., 3]." "Definition 1 (Dependency graph). $\mathcal G$ is a dependency graph if for all disjoint sets $\mathcal V_1, \mathcal V_2 \subset \mathcal V$ with no edge in $\mathcal E$ connecting a vertex in $\mathcal V_1$ to a vertex in $\mathcal V_2$, the set $\{Y_i : i \in \mathcal V_1\}$ is independent from the set $\{Y_j : j \in \mathcal V_2\}$."
(S2) Observation. p. 2240 (PDF p. 3): "Suppose $\mathcal G$ is a dependency graph and we observe a subset $\mathcal V_S \subseteq \mathcal V$, where $|\mathcal V_S| = n$. Label these observed vertices $1, \ldots, n$, and label the unobserved vertices in $\mathcal V \setminus \mathcal V_S$ arbitrarily by $n+1, \ldots, N$. For each $i \in \mathcal V_S$, we observe the outcomes $Y_1, \ldots, Y_n$, a fixed vector of coefficients $\theta = \theta_1, \ldots, \theta_n$, and the degrees $d_i = |\{j : \{i,j\} \in \mathcal E\}|$ for each $i \in \mathcal V_S$." "Definition 2 (Induced subgraph). For a set of vertices $\mathcal V_S \subseteq \mathcal V$, the induced subgraph in $\mathcal G$ is $\mathcal G_S = (\mathcal V_S, \mathcal E_S)$, where $\mathcal E_S = \{\{i,j\} : i \in \mathcal V_S,\ j \in \mathcal V_S,\ \text{and } \{i,j\} \in \mathcal E\}$." "Let $\mathcal G_S = (\mathcal V_S, \mathcal E_S)$ be the induced subgraph of the observed vertices $\mathcal V_S$. It follows that $\mathcal G_S$ is also a dependency graph. Let $\mathcal G_R = (\mathcal V_S, \mathcal E_R)$ be a subgraph of $\mathcal G_S$, consisting of all the observed vertices in $\mathcal V_S$, and a subset of the edges in $\mathcal E_S$." "Assumption 1 (Observed data). We observe the random outcomes $Y_1, \ldots, Y_n$, the fixed degrees $d_1, \ldots, d_n$, the fixed coefficients $\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_n$, and the fixed recruitment graph $\mathcal G_R$." "Let $Y = (Y_1, \ldots, Y_n)$, $d = (d_1, \ldots, d_n)$, and denote the observed data as $Z = (Y, d, \theta, \mathcal G_R)$."
(S3) Estimator and target. p. 2240 (PDF p. 3): "Definition 3 (Linear unbiased estimator (LUE)). An estimator $\hat\beta$ is a linear unbiased estimator (LUE) of $\beta$ if $\hat\beta = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in \mathcal V_S} \theta_i Y_i$ where $\mathrm{E}[\hat\beta] = \beta$." p. 2241 (PDF p. 4): "In what follows, we wish to conduct inference on $\beta$ given $Z$. We proceed by constructing conservative estimators of $\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) = \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i \in \mathcal V_S}^{n}\sum_{j \in \mathcal V_S}^{n} \theta_i\theta_j\,\mathrm{cov}(Y_i, Y_j)$."
(S4) Compatible adjacency matrices. p. 2241 (PDF p. 4): "We consider a class of variance estimators that depend on knowledge of $\mathcal G_S$, whose structure is represented by an $n \times n$ binary symmetric zero-diagonal adjacency matrix in which rows and columns are ordered by the indices $1, \ldots, n$ of the vertices in $\mathcal V_S$." "Definition 4 (Compatibility). The $n \times n$ binary symmetric adjacency matrix $A$ is compatible with the observed data $Z$ if for each $\{i,j\} \in \mathcal E_R$, $A_{ij} = A_{ji} = 1$, and for each $i \in \mathcal V_S$, $\sum_{j \in \mathcal V_S} A_{ij} \le d_i$." "The last condition in Definition 4 requires that the degree of $i$ in the subgraph $\mathcal G_S$ not be greater than its degree in the full graph $\mathcal G$. Let $A^{\mathcal O} = \{A^{\mathcal O}_{ij}\}$ be the true $n \times n$ adjacency matrix of $\mathcal G_S$, where $A^{\mathcal O}_{ij} = 1$ if $\{i,j\} \in \mathcal E_S$ for $i, j \in \mathcal V_S$ and 0 otherwise. Let $\mathcal A(Z) = \{A : A \text{ is compatible with } Z\}$ in the sense of Definition 4; it is clear that $A^{\mathcal O} \in \mathcal A(Z)$." "Definition 5 (Oracle estimator). For a family of variance estimators $\widehat V(A;Z)$ defined for $A \in \mathcal A(Z)$, the oracle estimator is $\widehat V(A^{\mathcal O};Z)$." "For a variance estimator $\widehat V(A;Z)$, define the set $\mathcal A^m = \{A \in \mathcal A(Z) : \widehat V(A;Z) \text{ is maximized}\}$." "Definition 6 (Maximal compatible estimator). Let $A^m \in \mathcal A^m$. The maximal compatible estimator is $\widehat V(A^m;Z)$."
(S5) Asymptotic scaling. p. 2242 (PDF p. 5): "Assumption 2 (Asymptotic scaling). Consider the sequence $(\mathcal G, Z)_n$ of nested graphs $\mathcal G$ and observed data $Z = (\mathcal G_R, Y, d)$, where $\mathcal G_R = (\mathcal V_S, \mathcal E_R)$, $|\mathcal V_S| = n$, and $|\mathcal V| = N_n \ge n$. Assume there exist finite, positive constants $c_1$, $c_2$ such that for every element $(\mathcal G, Z)_n$, $\Pr(|\theta_i Y_i - \beta| > c_1) = 0, \forall i \in \mathcal V_S$ (bounded outcome values) and $\sum_{j \in \mathcal V_S} A^{\mathcal O}_{ij} \le c_2, \forall i \in \mathcal V_S$ (bounded degrees in dependency graph). Further assume there exists a finite, positive constant $c_3$ such that $\lim_{n\to\infty} n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) = c_3$ (nondegenerate limiting variance). Finally, assume $c_4$ is a finite positive constant such that $|\theta_i| < c_4$."
(S6) General estimator. p. 2242 (PDF p. 5): "Define the plug-in sample variance $\hat\sigma_\theta^2 = n^{-1}\sum_{i \in \mathcal V_S}(\theta_i Y_i - \hat\beta)^2$, and the estimator $\widehat V_1(A;Z) = \frac{1}{n^2}\left[n\hat\sigma_\theta^2 + \sum_{i \in \mathcal V_S}\sum_{j \in \mathcal V_S} A_{ij}(\theta_i Y_i - \hat\beta)(\theta_j Y_j - \hat\beta)\right]$. (3.1)" p. 2244 (PDF p. 7): "Let $\mathcal A_1^m = \{A \in \mathcal A(Z) : \widehat V_1(A;Z) \text{ is maximized}\}$ be the set of compatible adjacency matrices that maximize $\widehat V_1(A;Z)$. Let $\Theta = \mathrm{diag}(\theta)$ be the $n \times n$ matrix with $\Theta_{ii} = \theta_i$ and $\Theta_{ij} = 0$ for $i \ne j$."
(S7) Homoskedastic estimators. p. 2246 (PDF p. 9): "Assumption 3 (Homoskedasticity). $\mathrm{var}(\theta_i Y_i) = \mathrm{var}(\theta_j Y_j), \forall i, j \in \mathcal V$." "A bound that is relatively computationally simple to compute can be derived by noting that when $\mathrm{var}(\theta_i Y_i) = \sigma_\theta^2$, $\mathrm{cov}(\theta_i Y_i, \theta_j Y_j) \le \sigma_\theta^2 A^{\mathcal O}_{ij}$. Define the estimator $\widehat V_2(A;Z) = \frac{\hat\sigma_\theta^2}{n}\left[1 + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in \mathcal V_S}\sum_{j \in \mathcal V_S} A_{ij}\right]$. (3.7)" "Define $\mathcal A_2^m = \{A \in \mathcal A(Z) : \widehat V_2(A;Z) \text{ is maximized}\}$, and let $A^m \in \mathcal A_2^m$." pp. 2246–2247 (PDF pp. 9–10): "For $i \in \mathcal V_S$, let $d_i' = \min\{d_i, n-1\}$ be the degree of $i$ in $\mathcal G$, truncated at $n-1$. Let $\widehat V_2'(Z) = \frac{\hat\sigma_\theta^2}{n}\left[1 + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in \mathcal V_S} d_i'\right]$. (3.9)"
(S8) Degree bounds in place of degrees. p. 2248 (PDF p. 11): "Alternatively, we may not have full knowledge of the degrees $d = (d_1, \ldots, d_n)$, and instead have only an upper bound $d_i^*$ for each $d_i$, or a global upper bound $d_i \le d^*$ for all $i = 1, \ldots, n$. Conservative variance estimation in both of these cases can be achieved (by substituting $d_i^*$ or $d^*$ for $d_i$) with no change to the programs (3.5) and (3.8) or to the asymptotic results given here. When no information about $\mathcal G_R$ or the degrees $d$ is available, setting every $d_i = d^* = n-1$ delivers a maximally conservative upper bound."
(S9) Audit notation, not in the paper (from the validators' derivations and the from-scratch check of the correction). $X_i = \theta_i Y_i$; $\mu_i = \mathrm{E}[X_i]$; $\delta_i = \mu_i - \beta$ (so $\sum_i \delta_i = 0$ by Definition 3, but no $\delta_i$ need be 0); $u_i = X_i - \mu_i$; $e_i = X_i - \hat\beta$; $C$ is the $n \times n$ covariance matrix of $(X_1, \ldots, X_n)$; $S = I + A^{\mathcal O}$; $b_n = \frac{1}{n}\delta^{\mathsf T}(I + A^{\mathcal O})\delta = \frac{1}{n}\left[\sum_i \delta_i^2 + \sum_i\sum_j A^{\mathcal O}_{ij}\delta_i\delta_j\right]$; for a symmetric $n \times n$ matrix $M$, $\widehat V_M = \frac{1}{n^2}e^{\mathsf T}Me$, so that $\widehat V_1(A;Z) = \widehat V_{I+A}$; for an adjacency matrix $A$, $d_i^A = \sum_j A_{ij}$ and $D_A = \mathrm{diag}(d_i^A)$; $D' = \mathrm{diag}(d_i')$. By Definition 1, $C_{ij} = 0$ whenever $i \ne j$ and $A^{\mathcal O}_{ij} = 0$, so $n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) = \frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\{(I + A^{\mathcal O})C\}$.
(S10) Reading conventions (for the formalizer; conventions, not quotations). (a) At each $n$ there is one probability space carrying the outcomes; $\mathrm{E}$, $\mathrm{var}$, $\mathrm{cov}$, $\Pr$ refer to their joint law. The graphs, the degrees $d_i$ and the coefficients $\theta_i$ are non-random; they and $\beta = \mathrm{E}[\hat\beta]$ may depend on $n$ (the regression weights of Section 2 do). (b) The constants $c_1, \ldots, c_4$ of Assumption 2 do not depend on $n$, and its conditions hold for every $n$ and every $i \in \mathcal V_S$. (c) "$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr(\cdot > \epsilon) = 0$ for any $\epsilon > 0$" is a statement about the sequence indexed by $n$. (d) "will have (at least) $100(1-\alpha)\%$ coverage for $\beta$ in large $n$" is read as: the limit (limit inferior) of $\Pr(|\hat\beta - \beta| \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V})$ equals (is at least) $1 - \alpha$, for $0 < \alpha < 1$, with $z_{1-\alpha/2} = \Phi^{-1}(1 - \alpha/2)$. The printed interval is undefined when $\widehat V < 0$, which can happen for $\widehat V_1$; the corrected statements use $\max\{\widehat V, 0\}$. (e) Double sums over $i, j \in \mathcal V_S$ are over ordered pairs. (f) In (3.5), $\Theta Y - \hat\beta$ is the vector with entries $\theta_i Y_i - \hat\beta$, $1$ is the vector of ones, and $\preceq$, $\succeq$ are element-wise $\le$, $\ge$ (the print says "less-than"; P011-N001). (g) Assumption 3 is used only for $i, j \in \mathcal V_S$ (P011-N001); the common variance, which may depend on $n$, is written $\sigma_\theta^2$ in the paper and $\sigma_n^2$ in the corrected statements. (h) "Valid constraints" means $\mathcal E_R \subseteq \mathcal E_S$ and $d_i \ge \sum_j A^{\mathcal O}_{ij}$ for every $i \in \mathcal V_S$ (true degrees in $\mathcal G$, or upper bounds on them as in (S8)), which gives $A^{\mathcal O} \in \mathcal A(Z)$. (i) In Corollaries 1 and 3, $A^m \in \mathcal A_1^m$; in Lemma 1 and Corollaries 2 and 4, $A^m \in \mathcal A_2^m$.
Scope of the list. Targets come from two sources. (1) Headline claims P011-H1 to P011-H7 are mathematical and are targets (H1 and H4 are false as printed and appear as results touched by P011-E001; H2, H3, H5, H6 and the formal part of H7 appear as headline results). P011-H8 (the R package implements the method) is a statement about software and is not a target. (2) Confirmed errors whose correction changes a mathematical statement, a formula or a proof step: P011-E001 (Critical; targets T1–T10, T31–T33, with the corrected statements taken from the from-scratch check runs/P011/correction-recheck/recheck.json, as NOTES-FOR-AGENTS.md directs), P011-E004 (Moderate; T11, T12, T34), P011-E002 (Moderate; T13, T14, T30), P011-N006 (Moderate; an interpretive finding about the package vignette and README that rests on an exact counterexample; T15, T16, T35), and the Minor errors P011-E003 (T17, T18), P011-E005 (T19, T20), P011-E006 (T21), P011-E007 (T22, T23), P011-N001 (T24) and P011-E015 (T25, T26; the package's variance helpers use divisor $n-1$ where the paper's formulas (3.1), (3.7), (3.9) use $n$, a wrong constant relative to the printed formulas). Not targets: P011-E009 and P011-N007 (misprinted words), P011-N002 (bibliography), P011-E011, P011-E013 and P011-E014 (the package stops with an error or does not check the solver status: no formula or statement to correct), P011-E012 (the help page and vignette name estimator (3.9) where the code returns (3.7) at the optimized graph; both formulas and Lemma 1, which relates them, are correct as printed and are target T28, so there is no mathematical statement to correct), P011-E010 (out of scope), P011-E008 (clarity note), P011-N003 and P011-N008 (undetermined), P011-N004 and P011-N005 (not confirmed).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Proposition 1, corrected for a known graph: the positive-part estimator (F4)
canonical_claim.location: Replaces the use of $\widehat V_1(A^{\mathcal O};Z)$ when the dependency graph is known, p. 2242 (PDF p. 5); not printed in the paper
canonical_claim.statement:
[Corrected statement, from the from-scratch check of the correction] Suppose $A^{\mathcal O}$ is known. Let $I + A^{\mathcal O} = \sum_k\lambda_kq_kq_k^{\mathsf T}$ be an orthonormal eigen-decomposition, $(I + A^{\mathcal O})_+ = \sum_k\max(\lambda_k, 0)\,q_kq_k^{\mathsf T}$ its positive part, and $\widehat V_P(Z) = \frac{1}{n^2}e^{\mathsf T}(I + A^{\mathcal O})_+e$ with $e_i = \theta_i Y_i - \hat\beta$.
(a) [finite] $(I + A^{\mathcal O})_+$ is positive semidefinite; $(I + A^{\mathcal O})_+ - (I + A^{\mathcal O}) = \sum_k\max(-\lambda_k, 0)\,q_kq_k^{\mathsf T}$ is positive semidefinite; $\|(I + A^{\mathcal O})_+\| \le 1 + \max_i\sum_j A^{\mathcal O}_{ij}$; hence in every sample $\widehat V_P(Z) \ge \max\{\widehat V_1(A^{\mathcal O};Z), 0\}$.
(b) [asymptotic] Under Assumption 2, for any $\epsilon > 0$ and any unit means $\mathrm{E}[\theta_i Y_i]$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr(n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) - n\widehat V_P(Z) > \epsilon) = 0$.
(c) [what is not claimed] $(I + A^{\mathcal O})_+$ is the positive semidefinite matrix nearest to $I + A^{\mathcal O}$ in Frobenius norm, but it is not a least positive semidefinite majorant in the Loewner order: for the four-cycle of P011-T1 and $\delta = (0, 1, -1, 0)$, $\delta^{\mathsf T}(I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}})_+\delta = 1$, while there is a symmetric $M$ with $M$ and $M - (I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}})$ both positive semidefinite and $\delta^{\mathsf T}M\delta = 3/5$. $\widehat V_P$ is not affine in $A$ and cannot serve as the linear objective of (3.6).
(d) [the four-cycle] For $A_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ of P011-T1 the eigenvalues of $I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ are $3, 1, 1, -1$, the eigenvalue $-1$ having eigenvector $\frac12(1, -1, 1, -1)$, and for all real $x$: $x^{\mathsf T}(I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}})_+x = x^{\mathsf T}(I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}})x + \frac14(x_1 - x_2 + x_3 - x_4)^2 = \frac34(x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + x_4)^2 + \frac12\left((x_1 - x_3)^2 + (x_2 - x_4)^2\right)$. In the example of P011-T1, $\mathrm{E}[n\widehat V_P(Z)] = 4 - \frac{12}{n}$ and $n\widehat V_P(Z) \to 4 = n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta)$ in probability.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: $A^{\mathcal O}$, Assumption 2: standing assumptions. $\widehat V_M$, $e$: audit notation (S9). The Loewner order: $M_1 \preceq_L M_2$ when $M_2 - M_1$ is positive semidefinite. $A_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ and the example are in P011-T1.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (1) Part (a), for each $n$. (2) P011-T4 (iv) with $M_n = (I + A^{\mathcal O})_+$, which is deterministic with norm at most $1 + c_2$, gives (b). (3) The polynomial identity in (d). (4) The alternative majorant of (c) is determined in exact_results.json (key positive_part_not_universal_minimum) through $N = M - (I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}}) = \begin{pmatrix}17/20&-1/4&1/4&-17/20\\-1/4&3/20&-3/20&1/4\\1/4&-3/20&3/20&-1/4\\-17/20&1/4&-1/4&17/20\end{pmatrix}$, with $\delta^{\mathsf T}(I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}})\delta = 0$ and $\delta^{\mathsf T}N\delta = 3/5$. (5) In P011-T1's example the alternating direction $(1, -1, 1, -1)$ carries the means and has zero noise variance ($s^{\mathsf T}(2I + A_{\mathrm{cyc}})s = 0$), which is why the limit in (d) equals the truth.
canonical_claim.note: repair.right_statement ("Known-graph F4 is also conservative") and statements 88-93, 114 of recheck.json; DERIVATIONS.md sections 4 and 8; Algebra.lean (positive_part_cycle, majorant_not_least). The draft called F4 "exact" in its Example A; the check corrects this to asymptotically exact (E[n V_P] = 4 - 12/n).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Corollaries 1 and 3 in the degree-only case: the maximized $\widehat V_1$ when no edges are known (Proposition 1B of the correction, as strengthened by the check)
canonical_claim.location: Corollary 1, p. 2245 (PDF p. 8); the degree-only case is the one described on p. 2248 (PDF p. 11)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Corrected statement, from the from-scratch check of the correction] Suppose no edges are known, $\mathcal E_R = \emptyset$, so that $\mathcal A(Z)$ is the set of binary symmetric zero-diagonal $A$ with $\sum_j A_{ij} \le d_i$ for every $i$, and let $A^m \in \mathcal A_1^m$ maximize $\widehat V_1(A;Z)$ over $\mathcal A(Z)$. Write $e_i = \theta_i Y_i - \hat\beta$, $B = \max_i|e_i|$, $d_i' = \min\{d_i, n-1\}$ and $\widehat V_Y'(Z) = \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_i(1 + d_i')e_i^2$ (P011-T5).
(a) [finite identity] For every binary symmetric zero-diagonal $A$: $e^{\mathsf T}Ae = \sum_i d_i^A e_i^2 - \sum_{i<j}A_{ij}(e_i - e_j)^2$.
(b) [finite bound] If $d_i' \le D$ for every $i$, with $D$ a nonnegative integer, then in every sample $0 \le n\widehat V_Y'(Z) - n\widehat V_1(A^m;Z) \le \frac{C_DB^2}{n}$, where $C_D = \sum_{d=1}^{D}(3d^2 + 2d)$.
(c) [asymptotic] Under Assumption 2, with $\mathcal E_R = \emptyset$ and valid degree bounds ($d_i \ge \sum_j A^{\mathcal O}_{ij}$; the supplied $d_i$ need not be bounded in $n$), for any $\epsilon > 0$ and any unit means $\mathrm{E}[\theta_i Y_i]$: $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr(n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) - n\widehat V_1(A^m;Z) > \epsilon) = 0$. So Corollary 1, and with it Corollary 3 (in the form of P011-T8), hold as printed when only degree information is used.
(d) [the equivalence in (b) needs bounded supplied degrees] Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be independent with $\Pr(X_i = 1) = \Pr(X_i = -1) = 1/2$, $\theta_i = 1$, empty dependency graph (Assumption 2 holds with $c_3 = 1$), $\mathcal E_R = \emptyset$ and supplied bounds $d_i = n - 1$. Then, on the event that $\hat\beta \ne \pm 1$, the maximizing graph joins all units with positive $e_i$ into one clique and all units with negative $e_i$ into another, and $\widehat V_1(A^m;Z) = \frac12(1 - \hat\beta^2)^2 \to \frac12$ while $\widehat V_Y'(Z) = 1 - \hat\beta^2 \to 1$ in probability (unscaled values).
(e) [the same comparison for the degree-corrected estimator] If $d_i' \le D$ for every $i$ and $\mathcal E_R = \emptyset$, then in every sample $0 \le \frac1n\sum_i\max(1, 2d_i')e_i^2 - n\widehat V_1^{+}(A^{m+};Z) \le \frac{B^2}{n}\sum_{d=1}^{D}(4d^2 + d)$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Definition 4, $\mathcal A_1^m$, (3.1), Assumption 2, (S8): standing assumptions. $\widehat V_Y'$, $\widehat V_1^{+}$, $A^{m+}$, $t_i$: P011-T5. $d_i^A = \sum_j A_{ij}$. Under Assumption 2, $B \le 2c_1$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (1) (a), by expanding $(e_i - e_j)^2$. (2) The upper bound $\widehat V_1(A;Z) \le \widehat V_Y'(Z)$ for compatible $A$ (P011-T5 (e)). (3) The construction for the lower bound in (b): for each $d \ge 1$, sort the units with $d_i' = d$ by $e_i$ and partition them into consecutive groups of $d + 1$; join each full group into a clique and leave the at most $d$ remaining units isolated; this $A$ is compatible when $\mathcal E_R = \emptyset$. By (a), $n^2\widehat V_Y'(Z) - n^2\widehat V_1(A;Z) = \sum_i(d_i' - d_i^A)e_i^2 + \sum_{i<j}A_{ij}(e_i - e_j)^2$; the first sum is at most $d^2B^2$ per class; with $\Delta_g$ the range of $e$ in full group $g$, $\sum_g\Delta_g \le 2B$, so $\sum_g\Delta_g^2 \le 4B^2$ and the second sum is at most $\frac12d(d + 1)\cdot 4B^2 = 2d(d + 1)B^2$ per class. (4) For (c): replace the bounds by $\tilde d_i = \min\{d_i', \lceil c_2\rceil\}$; the smaller compatible set still contains $A^{\mathcal O}$ and satisfies (b) with $D = \lceil c_2\rceil$, the closed-form bound with $\tilde d$ is asymptotically conservative (P011-T5 (h)), and the maximum over the original larger set dominates. (5) For (d): with $n_+ = n(1 + \hat\beta)/2$ units at $e = 1 - \hat\beta$ and $n_- = n(1 - \hat\beta)/2$ at $e = -1 - \hat\beta$, $\sum_i e_i^2 + e^{\mathsf T}Ae = (n_+(1 - \hat\beta))^2 + (n_-(1 + \hat\beta))^2 = \frac{n^2}{2}(1 - \hat\beta^2)^2$ for the two-clique graph, and $\frac1n\sum_i e_i^2 = 1 - \hat\beta^2$. (6) For (e): the same sorted-clique construction with unsaturated loss at most $(2d^2 - d)B^2$ and difference loss at most $2d(d + 1)B^2$ per class.
canonical_claim.note: repair.right_statement ("original max is conservative in the degree-only setting. With bounded supplied caps, original max and F3 differ by at most C_D B^2/n at n scale") and statements 34-44, 96, 97, 136 and 147 of recheck.json; errors_in_draft item 7; DERIVATIONS.md section 3 (equations D5, D7). This is what survives of headline claim P011-H4 for the paper's own estimator: with degree information only, the printed Corollary 1 is true; it fails once known edges restrict the compatible set (P011-T1, P011-T2).

canonical_claim.location: Corollary 1: p. 2245 (PDF p. 8); Corollary 3: p. 2248 (PDF p. 11); the sentence on p. 2246 (PDF p. 9) is deleted
canonical_claim.statement:
[Corrected statement, from the from-scratch check of the correction and the validators' repair] Let $\mathcal C$ be the following list of variance estimators, each with the condition under which it is on the list: (1) $\widehat V_1^{+}(A^{\mathcal O};Z)$, $\widehat V_1^{+}(A^{m+};Z)$, $\widehat V_Y'(Z)$ and $\min\{\widehat V_1^{+}(A^{m+};Z), \widehat V_Y'(Z)\}$ of P011-T5, under valid constraints; (2) $\widehat V_P(Z)$ of P011-T6, when $A^{\mathcal O}$ is known; (3) $\widehat V_1(A^m;Z)$ with $A^m \in \mathcal A_1^m$, when $\mathcal E_R = \emptyset$ and the degree bounds are valid (P011-T7); (4) $\widehat V_1(A^{\mathcal O};Z)$ and $\widehat V_1(A^m;Z)$ with $A^m \in \mathcal A_1^m$, under valid constraints, when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\delta^{\mathsf T}(I + A^{\mathcal O})\delta \ge 0$, in particular when $\mathrm{E}[\theta_i Y_i] = \beta$ for every $i \in \mathcal V_S$, or when $\mathcal G_S$ is a disjoint union of cliques for every $n$.
Corollary 1 (revised). Given Assumption 2, for every $\widehat V \in \mathcal C$ and any $\epsilon > 0$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr(n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) - n\widehat V(Z) > \epsilon) = 0$.
Corollary 3 (revised). Given Assumption 2, for every $\widehat V \in \mathcal C$ and every $0 < \alpha < 1$, $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\left(|\hat\beta - \beta| \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\max\{\widehat V(Z), 0\}}\right) \ge 1 - \alpha$.
The sentence on p. 2246, "Under homoskedasticity, the general estimator $\widehat V_1(A^m, Z)$ developed in Section 3.1 provides a conservative variance estimate", is deleted: Assumption 3 equalizes variances, not means, and the examples of P011-T1 and P011-T2 are homoskedastic. For $\widehat V_1(A^m;Z)$ with known edges and no condition on the unit means, neither conclusion holds in general (P011-T1, P011-T2).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Assumption 2, Definitions 4–6, (3.1): standing assumptions; reading conventions (S10)(d), (h). $\widehat V_1^{+}$, $A^{m+}$, $\widehat V_Y'$: P011-T5. $\widehat V_P$: P011-T6. $\delta$: audit notation (S9). The estimators in (1) and (2) are nonnegative, so the maximum with 0 matters only for (3) and (4).
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (1) In every sample $\widehat V_1(A^m;Z) \ge \widehat V_1(A^{\mathcal O};Z)$ because $A^{\mathcal O} \in \mathcal A(Z)$; with P011-T3 (v) this gives (4) of the list. (2) The coverage argument, for $T_n = n\widehat V$ with $\Pr(c_n - T_n > \epsilon) \to 0$ for every $\epsilon > 0$ and $c_n = n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) \to c_3 > 0$: put $U_n = \min\{\max\{T_n, 0\}, c_n\}$; then $0 \le c_n - U_n \le (c_n - T_n)_+$ in every sample, so $U_n - c_n \to 0$ in probability; by Lemma 2 (P011-T38) and Slutsky's theorem the interval with half-width $z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{U_n/n}$ has limiting coverage $1 - \alpha$; and the interval with half-width $z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\max\{T_n, 0\}/n}$ contains it in every sample.
canonical_claim.note: Statements 137-139 of recheck.json ("Corollaries 1 and 3 should be stated for the conservative corrected estimators and the degree-only original maximum"; "Delete the Section 3.2 claim that homoskedasticity alone makes original V1(A^m) conservative") and DERIVATIONS.md section 7; item (4) of the list is the validators' smallest repair (liminf b_n >= 0 is sufficient for Corollaries 1 and 3). The coverage argument is Proposition 3 (P011-T39) with the truncation at zero made explicit.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: The residual-centred version of $\widehat V_1$ when a mean model is available, with the regularity it needs
canonical_claim.location: Replaces the centring at $\hat\beta$ in (3.1) and (3.5), pp. 2242 and 2244 (PDF pp. 5 and 7), for the regression example of Section 2, pp. 2240–2241 (PDF pp. 3–4); not printed in the paper
canonical_claim.statement:
[Corrected statement, from the from-scratch check of the correction] Suppose in addition that $\mathrm{E}[Y_i] = x_i^{\mathsf T}\gamma$ for covariates $x_i \in \mathbb R^p$ with $p$ fixed, that the $x_i$ and the $\theta_i$ are bounded uniformly in $i$ and $n$, and that $\hat\gamma$ is an estimator with $\sqrt n\,(\hat\gamma - \gamma) = O_p(1)$. Let $z_i = \theta_i(Y_i - x_i^{\mathsf T}\gamma)$ and $r_i = \theta_i(Y_i - x_i^{\mathsf T}\hat\gamma) = z_i - \theta_i x_i^{\mathsf T}(\hat\gamma - \gamma)$, and define $\widehat V_1^{\mathrm{res}}(A;Z) = \frac{1}{n^2}r^{\mathsf T}(I + A)r$.
(a) The $z_i$ have mean zero and covariance matrix $C$; $\|r - z\|_\infty = O_p(n^{-1/2})$, $\|r - z\|_2 = O_p(1)$ and $\|z\|_2 = O_p(\sqrt n)$.
(b) [finite inequality] For every symmetric $M$: $|r^{\mathsf T}Mr - z^{\mathsf T}Mz| \le \|M\|\,\|r - z\|_2\left(2\|z\|_2 + \|r - z\|_2\right)$.
(c) Under Assumption 2: $n\widehat V_1^{\mathrm{res}}(A^{\mathcal O};Z) - n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) \to 0$ in probability; and for a maximizer $A^{m,\mathrm{res}}$ of $\widehat V_1^{\mathrm{res}}(A;Z)$ over $\mathcal A(Z)$ (valid constraints), $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr(n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) - n\widehat V_1^{\mathrm{res}}(A^{m,\mathrm{res}};Z) > \epsilon) = 0$ for any $\epsilon > 0$. More generally the conclusions hold whenever the weighted prediction error satisfies $\|r - z\|_2 = o_p(\sqrt n)$ and the summands $z_i$ are uniformly bounded.
(d) [the regularity is not implied by the paper's assumptions] Let $n = 4m$, regressors $(1, w_i)$ with $w = (1, 0, -1, 0)$ repeated, $R_i$ independent with $\Pr(R_i = 1) = \Pr(R_i = -1) = 1/2$, $\mathrm{E}[Y_i] = 0$, $Y_i = R_i$ if $w_i \ne 0$ and $Y_i = nR_i$ if $w_i = 0$. The OLS slope has weights $\theta_i = 2w_i$, so $X_i = 2w_iY_i$ is bounded by 2, the dependency graph is empty, $n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) = 2$ and $|\theta_i| < 3$: Assumption 2 holds for the slope and the linear mean model is exactly correct. Yet the fitted intercept $\bar Y$ has variance $\frac n2 + \frac{1}{2n}$, and with OLS residuals $\mathrm{E}[n\widehat V_1^{\mathrm{res}}(A^{\mathcal O};Z)] = n + 2 - \frac7n$ ($= 17/4$ at $n = 4$ and $73/8$ at $n = 8$), where $n\widehat V_1^{\mathrm{res}}(A^{\mathcal O};Z) = \frac4n\sum_{i: w_i \ne 0}(Y_i - \bar Y - w_i\hat b)^2$ and $\hat b = \frac2n\sum_i w_iY_i$; the estimate is not consistent for 2.
(e) [a wrong mean model] If there is a deterministic $\gamma_\ast$ such that, with $r_i^\ast = \theta_i(Y_i - x_i^{\mathsf T}\gamma_\ast)$, $\|r - r^\ast\|_2 = o_p(\sqrt n)$ and the $r_i^\ast$ are uniformly bounded, then $n\widehat V_1^{\mathrm{res}}(A^{\mathcal O};Z) - n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) - \frac1n\eta^{\mathsf T}(I + A^{\mathcal O})\eta \to 0$ in probability, with $\eta_i = \mathrm{E}[X_i] - \theta_i x_i^{\mathsf T}\gamma_\ast$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Assumption 2, Definitions 4–6: standing assumptions; $C$, $X_i$: audit notation (S9). $O_p$ and $o_p$ are with respect to $n \to \infty$. In (d) the "paper's assumptions" are Assumption 2 for the slope's weights and the linear mean model of p. 2240; the outcomes $Y_i$ themselves are not bounded there, only $\theta_i Y_i$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (1) (b), for each $n$, from $r^{\mathsf T}Mr - z^{\mathsf T}Mz = (r - z)^{\mathsf T}M(r + z)$. (2) $\mathrm{E}\left[\frac1n z^{\mathsf T}(I + A^{\mathcal O})z\right] = \frac1n\mathrm{tr}\{(I + A^{\mathcal O})C\} = n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta)$, with no centring term because $\mathrm{E}[z_i] = 0$; its variance is $O(1/n)$ by the local-dependence count of P011-T4. (3) $\|I + A^{\mathcal O}\| \le 1 + c_2$. (4) For (d), with $a = \bar Y$ and $\hat b$ as stated: $\mathrm{E}\left[\sum_{i: w_i \ne 0}Y_i^2\right] = n/2$, $\mathrm{E}\left[a\sum_{i: w_i \ne 0}Y_i\right] = 1/2$, $\mathrm{E}\left[\hat b\sum_i w_iY_i\right] = 1$, $\mathrm{E}[a^2] = \frac n2 + \frac{1}{2n}$, $\mathrm{E}[\hat b^2] = 2/n$; exact enumeration at $n = 4$ (16 states) and $n = 8$ (256 states) in exact_results.json (key OLS_missing_regularity).
canonical_claim.note: repair.right_statement ("Residual oracle consistency requires weighted fitted-mean error o_p(sqrt(n)) in l2 and bounded limiting residual summands; line 87's root-n/bounded-covariate conditions suffice") and statements 99-104, 107, 108 of recheck.json; errors_in_draft item 4; DERIVATIONS.md section 6. The draft said the paper's OLS example needs no extra assumption for this route; the check marks that incorrect, and (d) is its counterexample to the draft, not to a printed statement. The OLS-specific sufficient conditions are in P011-T16.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Why consistency cannot be kept for arbitrary unit means: no estimator is consistent at the $n$-scaled level over all bounded mean patterns
canonical_claim.location: Bears on the abstract, p. 2238 (PDF p. 1) ("We establish the consistency of an oracle variance estimator when a dependency graph is known") and Proposition 1, p. 2242 (PDF p. 5); not printed in the paper
canonical_claim.statement:
[Corrected statement, from the from-scratch check of the correction] Fix $a > 0$ and $b > 0$, and let $\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2, \ldots$ be independent with $\Pr(\varepsilon_i = 1) = \Pr(\varepsilon_i = -1) = 1/2$. For each deterministic sequence $s = (s_1, s_2, \ldots) \in \{-1, 1\}^{\mathbb N}$ let $P_s$ be the model $X_i = a s_i + b\varepsilon_i$ with $\theta_i = 1$ and the empty dependency graph. Under $P_s$: $\mathrm{E}[X_i] = a s_i$, $\beta = \beta_n = \frac an\sum_{i \le n}s_i$, $|X_i - \beta_n| \le 2a + b$, and $n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) = b^2$ for every $n$; Assumption 2 holds with $c_1 = 2a + b$, $c_3 = b^2$. Let $\bar P$ be the model in which $s_1, s_2, \ldots$ are themselves independent with $\Pr(s_i = 1) = \Pr(s_i = -1) = 1/2$ and independent of the $\varepsilon_i$: under $\bar P$ the $X_i$ are independent with mean 0, $\beta = 0$, and $n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) = a^2 + b^2$; Assumption 2 holds with $c_1 = a + b$, $c_3 = a^2 + b^2$.
(i) For each $n$, the law of $(X_1, \ldots, X_n)$ under $\bar P$ is the average over $s \in \{-1, 1\}^n$, with weights $2^{-n}$, of its laws under $P_s$.
(ii) There is no sequence of statistics $T_n = T_n(X_1, \ldots, X_n)$ such that $T_n \to b^2$ in probability under $P_s$ for every deterministic $s$ and $T_n \to a^2 + b^2$ in probability under $\bar P$. Consequently no variance estimator $\widehat V$ computed from the observed data satisfies $n\widehat V - n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) \to 0$ in probability for every sequence of models that satisfies the paper's assumptions.
(iii) If $T_n$ is conservative under $\bar P$, i.e. $\Pr(a^2 + b^2 - T_n > \epsilon) \to 0$ for every $\epsilon > 0$, then it is not true that $T_n \to b^2$ in probability under $P_s$ for every $s$: a guarantee that holds for all mean patterns costs width on some of them.
(iv) [what is not claimed] Unscaled consistency for $\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta)$ is trivial (the statistic 0 has it, because $\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) = O(1/n)$); and with additional structure, such as known sampling probabilities in a design-based setting, an unbiased variance estimator can exist.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Assumption 2 and Definition 3: standing assumptions. All models here have $\theta_i = 1$, $\mathcal G$ edgeless, $A^{\mathcal O} = 0$ and $d_i = 0$, so the observed data are $(X_1, \ldots, X_n)$ together with fixed, uninformative graph data. "Consistent at the $n$-scaled level" means $n\widehat V - n\,\mathrm{var}(\hat\beta) \to 0$ in probability.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (1) (i), exactly, for each $n$. (2) Under $P_s$, $\mathrm{var}(X_i) = b^2$; under $\bar P$, $\mathrm{var}(X_i) = a^2 + b^2$. (3) The argument for (ii): if $T_n \to b^2$ in probability under every $P_s$, then for each $\epsilon > 0$ the functions $s \mapsto P_s(|T_n - b^2| > \epsilon)$ are bounded by 1 and tend to 0 pointwise on $\{-1, 1\}^{\mathbb N}$, so by (i) and bounded convergence $\bar P(|T_n - b^2| > \epsilon) \to 0$, which contradicts $T_n \to a^2 + b^2$ under $\bar P$ since $a^2 > 0$. The quantifier over every deterministic infinite sequence is what makes the interchange of the mixture and the limit valid.
canonical_claim.note: Statements 49 (verdict incorrect as drafted: "No estimator can be consistent for Var(bhat) without restrictions on means"; corrected to n-scaled or relative consistency over the unrestricted bounded mean class), 50-56 and 151 of recheck.json; errors_in_draft item 2; DERIVATIONS.md section 5. This is the formal content of the repair cost recorded for P011-E001 (weaker conclusion): the corrected estimators of P011-T5 to P011-T7 are conservative, not consistent, and this target shows that consistency for all mean patterns is not available to any estimator.
